title: DenseOpenFinitenessComparison
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and P=(X,A) a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] with constructible torsion abelian sheaf A [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. Let U be a dense open of X, j its inclusion, and B=j_!j^*A [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Use the coefficient equivalence E from abelian groups to modules over ULift Z, defined by the inverse of the forgetful equivalence from Z-modules followed by restriction of scalars along ULift Z ≃ Z. Put F=E(A) and G=E(B). Write T(F) for the alternative that F has invertible-order torsion or is p-primary for a prime p=char(k) [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. C4(G) implies C4(F), and C5(G) implies C5(F). Under T(F) the reverse implications hold as well. Here C4 and C5 are the conditional invertible-order and proper constructible finiteness assertions [def-weil-pbc-C4], [def-weil-pbc-C5].

proof.text: Encode P.F as F. Apply isConstructibleSheaf_integral_iff with P.isTorsion and hP. The curve is Noetherian, so the open immersion is quasi-compact. Constructibility passes to module restriction and lower shriek; transfer it along the proved integral open-extension isomorphism to G.

The open-closed exact sequence makes the module counit J -> F mono. Composing with G = J gives a mono G -> F. Stalk functors preserve monos; the private helpers invertibleOrder_of_mono and primary_of_mono transfer the elementwise torsion conditions using injectivity and preservation of natural-number multiples.

Apply the integral unconditional finiteness equivalence. In the forward C4 direction, invertible torsion of F passes to G and the C4 assumption on G supplies all finite groups. In both proper directions the properness and constructibility hypotheses supply all finite groups on the assumed side; transfer through the equivalence. The reverse proper direction does not need its torsion alternative.

For reverse C4, split the torsion alternative. If F has invertible torsion, apply its conditional C4 and transfer finiteness. Otherwise F is p-primary with p=char(k), so G is p-primary. Under the requested invertible-order condition on G, each stalk element is killed by p^m and an integer n prime to p. The private isZero_of_primary_invertible helper uses coprimality to prove all stalks zero, then stalk conservativity to make G zero. The underlying abelian cohomology is subsingleton and hence finite.
